# Temple Scroll Column 50 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 50 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**50:1** Suppose a man has two wives — one he loves and one he does not — and both have given him sons.

**50:2** If the firstborn son belongs to the wife he does not love —

**50:3** when the time comes to divide his property among his sons, he must not give the rights of the firstborn to the son of the wife he loves instead of his actual firstborn son.

**50:4** He must recognize the firstborn rights of his older son by giving him a double share of everything he owns. That son was the first sign of his father's strength, and the firstborn rights belong to him.

**50:5** If a man has two wives, one he loves and one he does not, and both bear him sons, he must not rearrange the birth order.

**50:6** If the firstborn is the son of the unloved wife, the father must not promote the son of the loved wife to firstborn status over the true firstborn.

**50:7** The firstborn rights belong to the older son — he is the first sign of his father's strength.

**50:8** Suppose a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who refuses to obey either his father or his mother.

**50:9** They have disciplined him, but he still will not listen.

**50:10** His father and mother must take hold of him and bring him to the elders at the town gate.

**50:11** If a man has a stubborn, rebellious son who will not obey his father or mother, and refuses to change even after discipline —

**50:12** his parents must tell the elders of the town: This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious. He will not obey us. He is a wastrel and a drunk.

**50:13** Then all the men of the town must stone him to death. You must purge the evil from among you. All Israel will hear about it and be afraid.

**50:14** If someone commits a crime punishable by death and is executed, and the body is hung on a pole —

**50:15** the body must not stay on the pole overnight. Bury it that same day, because a body left hanging is an insult to God. Do not defile the land the LORD your God is giving you.

**50:16** If you see your neighbor's ox or sheep wandering off, do not look the other way. Make sure to take them back to their owner.

---

*PNEUMA notes: This column presents three interconnected laws about family and community order. The firstborn law protects inheritance rights from emotional favoritism — a father cannot disinherit a son just because he prefers the other wife. The rebellious son law is extreme by modern standards but represents the community's ultimate check on destructive behavior. The hanging law (vv. 14-15) insists on dignity even for the executed — Paul later cited this text in Galatians 3:13 regarding Christ's crucifixion.*
